facts.raw_span: 2-year history of progressively worsening fever
weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough
chronic lower back pain without neurologic deficits
painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux
two sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics, both negative
Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL
ESR >130 mm/hr
CRP 113 mg/L
induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
Chest radiograph showed bilateral reticular-nodular opacities
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression

concepts.why: The patient has a trace positive GeneXpert test for MTB, a biopsy showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with an acid-fast bacillus, and imaging findings consistent with spinal and pulmonary TB.
The patient has chronic lower back pain and imaging findings consistent with contiguous spondylitis and discitis, which are characteristic of Pott's disease.

The patient has a positive GeneXpert test for MTB, bilateral reticular-nodular opacities on chest radiograph, and systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss, which are consistent with miliary tuberculosis.

The patient has a painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux, which is consistent with tuberculous osteomyelitis, and a biopsy showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with an acid-fast bacillus.
The patient has abnormal urine tests, including proteinuria and hematuria, which are consistent with renal tuberculosis, and systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss.
The patient has systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, and night sweats, and evidence of tuberculosis in multiple organs, including the lungs, spine, and kidneys.

rationales.F01: The patient's 2-year history of progressively worsening fever is consistent with a chronic infection such as tuberculosis.
rationales.F03: The patient's chronic lower back pain without neurologic deficits is consistent with Pott's disease or tuberculous osteomyelitis.
rationales.F09: The induced sputum being trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert is a strong indicator of tuberculosis.

rationales.F12: The MRI of the spine revealing contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression is consistent with Pott's disease or tuberculous osteomyelitis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of progressively worsening fever, weight loss, night sweats, and dry cough, along with the presence of MTB in the induced sputum and biopsy of the toe ulcer, and the involvement of multiple systems (pulmonary, skeletal, and possibly renal), best supports the diagnosis of systemic tuberculosis.
